All forms so listed will be eligible for expenditure of funds for necessary purposes Including land acquisition, research, and propagation. Under the present Act, separate lists of native and foreign endangered wildlife are maintained. The proposed legislation provides for only a single list of endangered wildlife of the world. For those species listed as endangered it will be indicated, among other things, whether they are (1) threatened with extinction or (2) likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction over all or a portion of their ranges, and the portions of the ranges where these conditions exist. The resulting list, in effect, divides endangered species into two groups, those species that are "threatened" and those that are "likely to become threatened." The latter group is treated separately in the legislation. 1/
Presently any interested person may appeal for a change in the endangered species list simply by submitting a request to the Secretary. Under the proposed legislation the appeal must be in the form of a petition for a review accompanied by substantial evidence to warrant such a review. Such a change will free the Secretary from an obligation to conduct a costly, time-consuming investigation in response to a poorly-conceived appeal.
At the present time shipments of wildlife or wildlife products that may be illicit under provisions of the Act may be transshipped through the United States without being subject to examination of U.S. customs agents.
